title: Comparing text and trees (diff / patch)
intro: Work from the module directory. Fixtures: **`left.txt`**, **`right.txt`**, **`ws_left.txt`**, **`ws_right.txt`**, **`same_a.txt`**, **`same_b.txt`**, **`y1.txt`**, **`y2.txt`**, **`m12.patch`**, **`patchset/`**, **`tree_l/`**, **`tree_r/`**, **`tree_ln/`**, **`tree_rn/`**. Extract or modify only under **`work/`**.

questions.prompt: **`left.txt`** and **`right.txt`** differ by exactly one change. Run a unified diff between them. How many lines in the diff output start with `+` but are not file headers (not `+++`)?
Using the same unified diff from the previous question, how many lines start with `-` but are not headers (not `---`)?
Print the range header line from that unified diff (the line starting with `@@`).

The directory trees **`tree_l/`** and **`tree_r/`** are mostly identical but one file differs. Compare them recursively for differences only. Which file differs? Give its path relative to either tree root.
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
diff -rq tree_l tree_r
```

The output line `Files tree_l/sub/b.txt and tree_r/sub/b.txt differ` identifies the changed file.

questions.prompt: **`ws_left.txt`** and **`ws_right.txt`** appear different but only differ in whitespace. Compare them with whitespace differences ignored. What is the exit code?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
diff -w ws_left.txt ws_right.txt; echo $?
```

`-w` ignores all whitespace differences; exit code `0` means no meaningful difference was found.

questions.prompt: **`same_a.txt`** and **`same_b.txt`** are byte-for-byte identical copies. Use a byte-comparison tool to verify this silently (suppressing output). What exit code does it return when files match?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
cmp -s same_a.txt same_b.txt; echo $?
```

`cmp -s` (silent) compares byte by byte and exits `0` if files are identical.

questions.prompt: Copy **`patchset/original.txt`** to `work/original.txt`, then apply **`m12.patch`** to the copy. What is the first line of the patched file?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
mkdir -p work
cp patchset/original.txt work/original.txt
( cd work && patch -p0 < ../m12.patch )
head -n1 work/original.txt
```

questions.prompt: Copy **`patchset/revised.txt`** to `work/revised.txt`, then apply **`m12.patch`** in reverse to convert it back to the original version. What is the first line of the result?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
cp patchset/revised.txt work/revised.txt
( cd work && patch -R -p0 < ../m12.patch )
head -n1 work/revised.txt
```

`-R` reverses the patch direction.

questions.prompt: The trees **`tree_ln/`** and **`tree_rn/`** are similar but one has an extra file the other lacks. Compare them recursively. Paste the exact output line diff prints about that file.
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
diff -r tree_ln tree_rn
```

When a file exists in one tree but not the other, `diff` reports `Only in <dir>: <filename>`.

questions.prompt: **`y1.txt`** contains one word and **`y2.txt`** contains a different word. Compare them side by side in a 20-character-wide display. Print the output line exactly, including the separator character.
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
diff -y -W 20 y1.txt y2.txt
```

`-y` enables side-by-side mode; `-W 20` sets the total display width. Changed lines are marked with `|` followed by a tab before the right-hand content.

questions.prompt: The directories `tree_secret_l/` and `tree_secret_r/` appear similar but one file has diverged. Use a recursive comparison to find which file differs, then read its content in the right-hand tree. What does it contain?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
diff -rq tree_secret_l tree_secret_r
# Files tree_secret_l/report/summary.txt and tree_secret_r/report/summary.txt differ
cat tree_secret_r/report/summary.txt
```

`diff -rq` reports changed files without showing the diff body — efficient for locating the diverged file. Reading the right-hand version reveals the updated content.

summaryMarkdown:
## Learning outcomes
- Generate unified diffs (`-u`) and read `+`/`-` hunks with context.
- Compare directories recursively (`-r`, `--no-dereference` where relevant).
- Apply patches with `patch -pN`; reverse with `-R`.
- Use color and side-by-side options where available (GNU vs BSD).

## Scope

**In scope:** text and tree diffs, patch application on copies. **Out of scope:** three-way merges (`diff3`, `git merge` internals) beyond mention.
